## Intro:

Quarto enables you to weave together content and executable code into a finished document. To learn more about Quarto see <https://quarto.org>.

You can write using the Visual editor, or the Source script in [Markdown](https://rmarkdown.rstudio.com/lesson-1.html)

In this case, we want to create a simple dynamic report, but more complex webpages can be build (e.g. <https://ibartomeus.github.io/CropPollinationModels/>)

## Steps:

### Read data

We will use here as an example fake data store in `/data`

When you click the **Render** button a document will be generated that includes both content and the output of embedded code. You can embed code like this:

```{r}
#| label: read and plot data
#| echo: true
#| warning: false

#read data
dat <- read.csv("data/example_dataset.csv")

#plot data
plot(dat$abundance ~ dat$size, las = 1)
```

Note that we want to show both the code and the output, so we tagged `echo: true`. The `echo: false` option disables the printing of code (only output is displayed). We don't want to see any warning (`false`).
